clue.text: Large fellow in female clothing, a case for Freud!

indicators.note: the large fellow sits in the female, who wraps round the pair like clothing

parts.note: a woman is a female person
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A big man has turned up dressed as a woman, which sounds like one for the psychoanalyst's couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' just pictures the woman wrapped round the inserted letters. The Wolf Man was the nickname of one of Freud's most famous patients, Sergei Pankejeff.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's published study of the Russian patient Pankejeff is known by this nickname, from his dream of wolves in a tree.

clue.text: Understanding Norman?

definitions.meaning: Norman ... was a British slapstick comedian and film star of the 1950s and 60s

explanation.definitionFit: Sound judgement is the abstract sense; the surname of the comic actor Norman is the other.

clue.text: Place and time to see problem eater

parts.note: a locus is a place or position

explanation.surface: A place and time are fixed for meeting someone with an eating disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem eater' suggests a person with an eating disorder; it is the crop-devouring insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarms of these grasshoppers eat crops bare, making them a notorious agricultural problem.

clue.text: Transference initially delivers housewives from worries

indicators.note: the transfer happens at the start, so the opening letter of the word is exchanged for another

parts.note: distresses as a verb means worries or upsets

explanation.surface: Freudian transference relieves stay-at-home wives of their anxieties.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter changes; the clue does not say which letter comes in, so the definition has to tell the solver it is M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress of the house is an old-fashioned title for the woman who runs a household, a wife.

clue.text: Mercenary Japanese erotic writer has Freud's positive support

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: Anais Nin was a French-American author famous for her erotica
Freud spoke German, in which yes is ja

explanation.surface: A Japanese soldier for hire relies on an erotic novelist and Freud's encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese agent trained in covert warfare, hired for espionage and assassination.

clue.text: Catholics' Oedipus complex

indicators.note: a complex is an intricate tangle, so the letters of the name before it are tangled up

explanation.surface: Freud's famous Oedipus complex seen as something peculiar to Roman Catholics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' pretends to be Freud's term in 'Oedipus complex' but is the anagram signal. The definition is possessive because Opus Dei is a Catholic organisation, used here like an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is a conservative organisation within the Roman Catholic Church, so it belongs to Catholics.

clue.text: It's suggestive of repression, by George!

definitions.text: It's suggestive of repression, by George!

parts.words: It's suggestive of repression, by George!
parts.note: describes an adjective for a state of repression, derived from the pen name of the author George who wrote of Big Brother

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something hints at repression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by George!' is an old exclamation of surprise, but here means coined from the writer George Orwell, whose Nineteen Eighty-Four depicts state repression; 'repression' teases the Freudian sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes totalitarian surveillance and control as in the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Libido is located in our genitals

indicators.note: located in means found inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Sex drive resides in the private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong desire or impulse, especially sexual, is a near synonym of the sex drive.

clue.text: A proverbially cold thing, heartless Doctor Laing cruelly rejected girl

indicators.note: heartless means with the centre removed, so the middle letters of the word go
cruelly suggests rough handling, so the letters left are knocked about
rejected means thrown out, so the abbreviation for girl is cast out

parts.note: G is a dictionary abbreviation for girl

explanation.surface: The psychiatrist R. D. Laing coldly spurns a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes CT from the middle of DOCTOR, leaving DOOR; 'rejected' drops G from LAING, and 'cruelly' turns LAIN into NAIL. R. D. Laing was a Scottish psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'dead as a doornail' makes it the type of something stone dead and cold.

clue.text: In retirement half lost mind, pretending to be grand

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters go backwards
half the word is lost, so the back two of its four letters drop

parts.note: posing as something is pretending to be it

explanation.surface: In old age, someone half out of their mind puts on airs of grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half lost' leaves MI from MIND; 'In retirement' turns it to IM.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposing building or person is impressive in size or manner, grand.

clue.text: Exhibits infantile behaviour, expressing unpleasantness

definitions.meaning: a baby draws milk or a thumb into the mouth
slang for saying something is awful, as in 'this situation is rubbish'

explanation.definitionFit: Babies feed by drawing on the breast, and in slang a bad thing is said to do the same, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Internet forum for discussing latest type of therapy

parts.note: the latest is the news, the most recent information
group therapy is treatment carried out with several patients together

explanation.surface: An online discussion board devoted to the newest fashion in psychotherapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Usenet discussion area where users post and reply on a topic is called by this compound name.

clue.text: Verbal degeneration following Oscar's brain disease can be noticed

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the earlier pieces

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
BSE, bovine spongiform encephalopathy, is mad cow disease, which attacks the brain

indicators.note: degeneration means falling apart into a worse state, so the word before it breaks up into new order

explanation.surface: A man called Oscar suffers a brain disease and his speech decline becomes plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like a patient's name; it is the phonetic-alphabet O. 'degeneration' signals the anagram, and 'following' puts the jumble last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something observable is perceptible, able to be seen or noticed.

clue.text: A lot of students' object of fixation

parts.note: the NUS, the National Union of Students, is the UK body representing a great many students

explanation.surface: Many students share an obsession with something.
explanation.walkthrough: Freud's anal stage gives the 'anal fixation' that makes this a fair definition. The NUS is the British students' union.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory, a person stuck at the anal stage of development is fixated on this part of the body.

clue.text: Rogue or cad, tart and saint, represent archetypes for Jung

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means behaving erratically, so the letters that follow go astray

explanation.surface: Jung saw figures such as the rogue, the cad, the tart and the saint as embodying archetypes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like one of the list of characters but is the anagram signal; 'represent' is a link. Jung saw the figures of the tarot pack as images of his archetypes.
explanation.definitionFit: Jung regarded the picture figures of the tarot deck, such as the Fool and the Magician, as embodiments of his archetypes.

clue.text: Bulimia's not unusually a diversion of sexual energy

indicators.note: unusually means in an unaccustomed way, so the letters before it are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Bulimia, unusually, is not a channelling of the sex drive elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges BULIMIAS and NOT; the apostrophe S counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian psychology, the redirection of sexual drives into socially valued activities is the technical term defined here.

clue.text: "Drug is to be cut back", one interrupts Lacan rudely

indicators.note: back means returned, so the letters are read in the other direction
cut means trimmed, so the last letter is cut off
interrupts means breaks into, so this letter goes inside the jumble
rudely means roughly, so the letters of the name are roughed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drug is to be reduced as someone rudely breaks in on the analyst Lacan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' and 'back' work together on 'to be'; 'rudely' jumbles the analyst's name and 'interrupts' puts one inside it. Jacques Lacan was a French psychoanalyst.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a botanical is a medicine or preparation derived from plants.

clue.text: Posh dons, boy and man, following the founder of psychoanalysis

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the boy wears the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Fred is a boy's name
U means upper-class, posh
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: Upper-class academics, young and old, follow Sigmund Freud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university lecturers but is a verb: FRED puts on U.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Sigmund Freud is described by the adjective formed from his surname.

clue.text: Firstly Bowlby lucidly explained neurotic habits evident in many a posh house

indicators.note: firstly tells you to take the first letter of each word that follows

parts.words: Bowlby lucidly explained neurotic habits evident in many

explanation.surface: John Bowlby clearly accounted for the nervous habits seen in many a grand home.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bowlby was a British psychiatrist known for attachment theory. Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire is the Duke of Marlborough's seat, birthplace of Churchill.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim Palace is a huge stately home in Oxfordshire, the archetypal grand country house.

clue.text: Dr A. Adler, not a well man, at last slowing down

indicators.note: Dr, short for doctor, is read as the verb to doctor, meaning to tamper with, so the letters are altered
at last picks the final letter of each of the words just before it

explanation.surface: Dr A. Adler, being an unwell man, is finally losing pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr' looks like Alfred Adler's title but is the verb 'doctor', signalling the anagram. 'at last' supplies the final letters of 'well' and 'man'; the 'a' before 'well' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallentando is the musical direction to slow gradually in tempo.

clue.text: Like 1 across in happy mood, described by Rank

indicators.note: describe can mean draw round, so one piece is drawn round the other

parts.note: a rank is a line, as of soldiers
up means cheerful, in good spirits

explanation.surface: Freud's colleague Otto Rank depicts a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like the psychoanalyst Otto Rank but means a line. The cross-reference is to the werewolf answer at 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means wolf-like, which fits a man who turns into a wolf.

clue.text: Therapists' freeing of sex offender is causing argument

indicators.note: freeing means releasing, so the offender is let out of the word

parts.note: a rapist is a sex offender

explanation.surface: Therapists who release a sex offender are causing controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freeing of' removes RAPIST from THERAPISTS, leaving THES.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward and argued for, an argument.

clue.text: They provide tea when you are briefly bipolar

parts.note: text-speak shortens 'you are' to the two letters U and R
having two poles, north and south, abbreviated N and S

explanation.surface: Tea arrives when you are suffering from bipolar disorder, in short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bipolar' looks like the mental illness but means the two poles of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea urns are large heated vessels that dispense hot water or tea at gatherings.

clue.text: Lying under psychoanalysis

definitions.meaning: lying down, reclining on a sofa
receiving treatment from an analyst, traditionally reclining on a sofa

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes reclining on a sofa, and idiomatically means being in therapy, as Freud's patients lay on one.

clue.text: Shrink's experience end to mental blocks

indicators.note: the letter blocks the word by standing in the middle of it

parts.note: to have something is to experience it, as in having a good time

indicators.note: end to picks out the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist's experience brings an end to mental blocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like slang for psychiatrist but is the verb; the apostrophe S is a link meaning has.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to cut it to half its size, reducing or making it smaller.

clue.text: Personality that radiates energy

definitions.meaning: a sun-like body in space giving out light and heat

explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is a famous name, and a sun is a luminous heavenly body pouring out light and heat.

clue.text: Unconscious, a client may be analysed just the same

parts.note: in Freudian theory the id is the unconscious part of the psyche

indicators.note: to analyse is to break something into parts, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A patient's unconscious may be studied by the analyst in exactly the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconscious' is the Freudian id, and 'may be analysed' signals the anagram of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are identical are exactly alike in every respect.

clue.text: They restrain toddlers' orally predominant periods

indicators.note: orally means by mouth, spoken, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: reigns are periods of rule or dominance

explanation.surface: Something about toddlers' predominantly oral stages of development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orally' teases Freud's oral stage but signals the sound. In Britain toddlers are often walked on a harness with straps called reins.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's harness with straps held by a parent is called by the same word as a horse's straps.

clue.text: Rebellious supermodel, a remunerative case for one?

indicators.note: rebellious means revolting, turning against, so the letters are turned round
a case holds something inside it, so the letters sit within the words

explanation.surface: A rebellious supermodel is a profitable client for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes LAREMUN from the run 'supermodeL A REMUNerative', and 'Rebellious' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an example of a figure or symbol standing for a number, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Consumers consume Seroxat primarily during annual holiday periods

indicators.note: to consume is to swallow up, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: consumers of food are eaters

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Shoppers take a lot of the antidepressant Seroxat over the spring holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Seroxat is a brand of the antidepressant paroxetine.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is a Christian festival with a public holiday each spring, and the plural covers several such years.
